title: WPSS/2000/2014 of Bhuwan Chandra Pandey Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No.2000 of 2014
Bhuwan Chandra Pandey
 ÖÖ. Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others
....Ö. Respondents
Mr. D.K. Joshi, Advocate for the petitioner-Bhuwan Chandra Pandey.
Ms. Seema Sirohi, Brief Holder for the State/respondent nos.1 to 4.
Ms. Shruti Joshi, Advocate for respondent no.5- Abhishek Pathak
.
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
 Having heard learned counsel for the parties, it
transpires that on 2.7.2014, the advertisement was
published from the office of District Tuberculosis Officer,
calling response of qualified candidates to apply for the
post of Senior Treatment Supervisor (STS). Application
forms were to be submitted within two weeks i.e. 17.7.2014
was the last date for receipt of applications. Not much
number of candidates, but only 28 could apply and they
were evaluated by way of testing them on the basis of
qualification possessed by them, as was adverted in the
publication nay the personal interview. Limiting only two
weeks for calling applications is utter haste in employment
matters and thus, reflects some unfair design on the part of
competent authority. The evaluation-sheet has been filed as
Annexure no.7 with the petition showing the comparative
chart of marks obtained by all the candidates including the
petitioner and the respondent no.5.
2. It was submitted that respondent no.5- Abhishek
Pathak was awarded -5- marks for the so-called experience
of more than two years in the field of Medical Social Work

2
whereas the petitioner was given zero mark despite having
experience certificate issued on 9.5.2009 by the competent
authority, albeit such was only for -10- months, but
looking to the credentials of both the candidates, contesting
herein for the same post, it is abundantly clear that the
certificate possessed by the petitioner is quite trustworthy
whereas the certificate, which was made the basis for
allotting -5- marks in favour of respondent no.5, is quite
vague, forged, pseudo in nature and un-speaking, issued
by some bogus institution without putting any legible
signature and date. Such certificate even does not disclose
the exact dates covered by respondent no.5 for gaining
such experience. That apart, respondent no.5 was a B.A.
regular student and in the session ended in July, 2013, he
completed his graduation as a regular student, then it is
not acceptable that contemporarily, he was gaining
experience which was a pre-requisite for awarding -5-
marks for the post. So, the appointing authority i.e. Chief
Medical Officer, Bageshwar, at the relevant time, for the
reasons best known to him, appears to have shown un-warranted favour in giving appointment to respondent
no.5,.
3. Having gone through the merits of the case, it is
further revealed that the petitioner certainly was having
much higher qualification in the field of Pharmacy and he
also got his degree in such field by a recognized University
no less than Hemwati Nandan Bahuguna Central
University, besides completing his Masters degree in the
subject of Social Work which was accorded to him by the
Uttarakhand Open University. He has registered himself as
a Pharmacist with Uttaranchal Pharmacy Council on
6.10.2006, whereas respondent no.5 was simply an Arts

3
graduate. In addition thereto, the allocation of -9- marks
out of -10- in interview to respondent no.5 is quite
discriminatory in comparison to -4- marks out of -10
allotted to the petitioner.
4. It is really appalling that respondent no.5, whose
academic record was also not of very good nature, attained
outstanding marks in the interview, relatively to other
candidates who could secure the range of -2- to -4- marks,
despite having better academic records. If all these things
are taken into consideration, then the respondent no.5 will
certainly be at quite lower pedestal in comparison of the
petitioner- Bhuwan Chandra Pandey.
5. It is further surprising that the petitioner,
though resident of Bageshwar, was allotted zero mark while
respondent no.5 was allotted -5- marks on this score.
6. The argument on behalf of respondents that at
the time of sending application, petitioner did not attach
his local resident certificate, is not acceptable for the
reason that if such document was not annexed by the
petitioner, then, at least, he should have been rendered an
opportunity to produce the same within a reasonable time.
7. In view of this Court, it is amply clear that the
appointment of respondent no.5, in August, 2014, has been
made by the Chief Medical Officer, Bageshwar, misusing
his post and official position and showing special favours to
the said respondent, wherefor he is reprimanded by this
Court. The Principal Secretary (Health) of the State is
hereby directed to make an adverse entry to that effect in
the character roll dossier of C.M.O., Bageshwar, who
appointed respondent no.5 and issued the appointment
letter in quite biased a manner.

4
8. In view of what has been stated hereinabove, the
petition is allowed in toto. The appointment given to
respondent no.5- Abhishek Pathak is hereby done away
with from immediate effect. The State counsel will
communicate the Chief Medical Officer, Bageshwar not to
permit respondent no.5 to work from tomorrow, and at the
same time, mandamus is issued directing the said
Authority (C.M.O.) to permit the petitioner to join against
the said post.
9. It is hereby further observed that in case the
Principal Secretary (Health) of the State deems fit in the
interest to discourage corruption in the matter of
appointments, then he would be at liberty to recover the
pay and other monetary benefits, drawn so far by
respondent no.5 at the cost of government exchequer, from
the salary of the Chief Medical Officer, Bageshwar, who was
posted there at the relevant time.
10. Let a certified copy of this judgment be sent to
the Chief Secretary of the State, who in turn, will refer it to
the Principal Secretary (Health) to ensure immediate
compliance of the above order.
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)
 29.05.2015
Rdang
